In a Grubbs ring-closing metathesis the two terminal vinyl groups (–CH=CH2) lose their terminal CH2 fragments as ethylene; the two internal alkene carbons that remain become the C=C atoms of the new ring.  
For an 8-carbon diene (octadiene) whose double bonds are at C1–C2 and C7–C8:

• the new alkene is formed between C2 and C7  
• the six ring atoms are C2-C3-C4-C5-C6-C7

Hence the substituents originally on C6, C5 and C4 will appear on ring carbons 3, 4 and 5, respectively, in the cyclohexene product.

We need the cyclohexene to carry  
– CH3 on ring C3 and C4 → the linear precursor must have CH3 on C6 and C5  
– i-Pr on ring C5 → the linear precursor must have i-Pr on C4.

Among the choices, only

4-isopropyl-5,6-dimethylocta-1,7-diene

has vinyl groups at C1 and C7 and exactly this pattern of substituents (i-Pr at C4, Me at C5 and C6).  
Ring-closing metathesis of this diene removes the terminal CH2 groups as ethylene and yields

5-isopropyl-3,4-dimethylcyclohex-1-ene.

Therefore the correct starting material is option (C).

Answer: C
